Nigerian archives, records, museum collections and digitisation context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian records management, archives, museum collections, cataloguing, conservation, digitisation, audio-visual preservation and public access
findings: The National Archives describes preservation, records-management training, digitisation and training collaborations for archivists and records officers.
National museum and film-archive sources describe collection documentation, cataloguing, imaging, conservation and audio-visual preservation.
source_summaries.limitations: These sources support records and collections practice but do not establish one universal museum, archive or commercial software stack.

source_summaries.name: National Bureau of Statistics Nigeria Labour Force Survey
NBTE National Occupational Standards and Federal TVET trade pathways
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian vocational and technical pathways including garment making, leather work, furniture and upholstery, food and beverage service, industrial automation, AI, backend web, health and safety and other occupational standards
findings: NBTE's current NOS catalogue names occupational standards and levels for garment making, leather work, furniture and upholstery, food and beverage service, industrial automation, AI, backend web and other trades.
The Federal TVET initiative describes accredited centres, practical skills, employment and entrepreneurship pathways.
source_summaries.limitations: An NOS or TVET pathway is evidence of a Nigerian training route, not a claim that every employer requires the listed level or that one trade credential is interchangeable with a degree or professional licence.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian automotive repair, vehicle engineering, EV and motorsport training context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian automobile repair and maintenance, electric and CNG vehicle training, automotive engineering design tools, vehicle inspection and motorsport officials and engineering pathways
findings: Government and NADDC sources describe nationwide automobile-maintenance, electric-vehicle, CNG and automotive software-capacity training.
ATCN describes Nigerian motorsport governance, driver/official training and an FIA engineering scholarship pathway.
source_summaries.limitations: These are sector training and ecosystem signals; they do not establish one universal automotive tool stack or a licence for every vehicle, motorsport or engineering role.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian Institute of Professional Administrators and Office Technology and Management
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian office administration, secretarial administration and office-technology professional training/certification
findings: NIPAS publishes professional certification and examination procedures for office administration and office-technology candidates.
source_summaries.limitations: This is a professional training/membership route, not a universal statutory licence for every office administrator.

source_summaries.name: SMEDAN Nigerian founder, MSME, entrepreneurship and business-development training context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian MSME capacity building, entrepreneurship training, business development, access to finance, market support and founder development
findings: SMEDAN describes entrepreneurship training, capacity building, finance, markets and founder support for Nigerian nano, micro and small enterprises.
source_summaries.limitations: This supports entrepreneurial and business-development foundations; it does not establish a universal founder credential, company-registration outcome or demand ranking for every management role.

source_summaries.name: COREN National Clean Energy Skills Certification Scheme
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian renewable-energy and energy-efficiency skills and certification
findings: COREN describes itself as the national certification body for clean-energy skills and reports revalidation of competency standards in July 2024 and a 2025 partnership with NEMSA for renewable-energy and energy-efficiency certification.
source_summaries.limitations: This supports clean-energy skills certification context; it is not a universal licence for every energy or electrical role.

source_summaries.name: Council for the Regulation of Engineering in Nigeria registration guidance
COREN 2026 engineering regulation and public-safety reforms
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian engineering practice, registration, public safety, project monitoring and anti-quackery context
findings: COREN's 2026 reforms emphasise qualified and registered practitioners, public safety, project monitoring and enforcement against unqualified engineering practice.
source_summaries.limitations: The source supports regulated-engineering context; it is not a personal registration requirement for every technician or non-engineering role in an engineering organisation.

source_summaries.name: COREN and Nigerian Society of Engineers
Nigerian health records registration and digital health information context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian health records officers, health-information management, registration and licensure, electronic content management, digital health, EMR/EHR, data quality and confidentiality
findings: The Federal Ministry of Health describes HRORBN registration, digital compliance and health-records workforce demand, and describes ECM and national digital-health/EMR direction.
source_summaries.limitations: The regulatory requirement applies to defined health-records practice; digital-health context does not make every medical, data or administrative role a registered health-records profession.

MDCN and MLSCN Nigerian medical, dental and laboratory registration and training context
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian medical and dental education, housemanship, professional registration, annual practice licensing, medical laboratory training, laboratory registration and continuing professional development
findings: MDCN publishes medical and dental education, accreditation, registration, practising-licence and CPD services.
MLSCN publishes medical-laboratory training, registration, licensure, laboratory accreditation and CPD services, including the 2025 ND curriculum.
source_summaries.limitations: The regulations apply to defined health professions and facilities; they do not establish a universal licence for every health-support, research, technology or administrative role.

source_summaries.name: 3 Million Technical Talent technical skills tracks
Choice Talents Lagos and Abuja Game Developer vacancy
source_summaries.scope: One Nigerian game-developer vacancy listing for Lagos and Abuja
findings: The listing asks for Unity or Unreal Engine, C# or C++, 2D/3D graphics, prototyping, animation, testing, Git, documentation and a game portfolio.
The listing also mentions AR, VR and MR as adjacent technologies.
source_summaries.limitations: This is one vacancy and must not be treated as a national ranking or universal requirement.

Esports Federation of Nigeria national esports programmes
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian competitive gaming, schools and university esports, broadcasting, refereeing, tournament operations and team programmes
findings: The federation described a National Esports Championship, Team Nigeria programme, schools and university league, and training for referees, broadcasters and tournament officials.
source_summaries.limitations: Federation programmes demonstrate ecosystem and role-family context; they do not establish national job volume or a mandatory credential.

source_summaries.name: Federal Ministry of Arts, Culture, Tourism and the Creative Economy gaming sector context
source_summaries.scope: Nigeria gaming, game development, esports and immersive creative economy
findings: Government identifies game development, esports and immersive experiences as a Nigerian creative-economy growth area.
The ministry describes local talent support, digital-skills development and job creation as sector objectives.
source_summaries.limitations: Sector policy context is not a count of vacancies and does not establish an individual licence or credential requirement.

source_summaries.name: Creative Economy Development Fund gaming and animation value-chain map
source_summaries.scope: Nigeria gaming and animation value chain
findings: The value chain distinguishes skill and content creation, production and post-production, marketing, and distribution and monetisation.
The map names training, animators, game programmers, game-development studios and mobile gaming platforms as ecosystem participants.
source_summaries.limitations: The value-chain map describes ecosystem categories, not role-level hiring volume or guaranteed employment.

source_summaries.name: Gameloft Nigeria careers and game-studio signal
source_summaries.scope: Nigeria game-studio and game-business career ecosystem
findings: Gameloft maintains a Nigeria careers presence and identifies studio, creative and business-development pathways.
source_summaries.limitations: The careers landing page is a studio signal, not a complete Nigerian vacancy census.

source_summaries.name: Jobberman Nigeria jobs

source_summaries.scope: Nigeria game-design and game-development search results
findings: The search surface included Nigerian and remote listings using titles such as game designer, game developer, Unity developer, Unreal gameplay developer and Python game developer.
source_summaries.limitations: A search-results page is a directional market signal, not a deduplicated vacancy dataset and not proof that all results remain open.

source_summaries.name: Maliyo Games Nigerian studio and career ecosystem
source_summaries.scope: Lagos-based mobile-game design, development, art, narrative and distribution
findings: Maliyo identifies Lagos as its headquarters and describes work spanning African stories, characters, environments, visuals, sound and mobile-game distribution.
The studio links to careers, GameUp Africa and junior-internship pathways.
source_summaries.limitations: Studio capability and career pathways do not imply that every named role is currently open.

findings: The value chain distinguishes skill and content creation, production and post-production, marketing, and distribution and monetisation.

source_summaries.limitations: The value-chain map describes ecosystem categories, not role-level hiring volume or guaranteed employment.

source_summaries.scope: Nigerian creative-media trades including film, audio, content, photography, animation, graphics, broadcasting, gaming and immersive technologies
findings: The Nigerian Film Corporation reported a July 2026 critique and validation workshop intended to develop National Occupational Standards for creative-media trades, including film production, audio production, content creation, digital photography, animation, digital graphics, broadcasting, gaming and immersive technologies.

source_summaries.limitations: These are ecosystem and training signals, not evidence of a national vacancy count or universal tool requirement.

source_summaries.name: Federal Ministry of Arts, Culture, Tourism and the Creative Economy gaming sector context
source_summaries.scope: Nigeria gaming, game development, esports and immersive creative economy
findings: Government identifies game development, esports and immersive experiences as a Nigerian creative-economy growth area.
The ministry describes local talent support, digital-skills development and job creation as sector objectives.
source_summaries.limitations: Sector policy context is not a count of vacancies and does not establish an individual licence or credential requirement.

source_summaries.name: Creative Economy Development Fund gaming and animation value-chain map
source_summaries.scope: Nigeria gaming and animation value chain
findings: The value chain distinguishes skill and content creation, production and post-production, marketing, and distribution and monetisation.
The map names training, animators, game programmers, game-development studios and mobile gaming platforms as ecosystem participants.
source_summaries.limitations: The value-chain map describes ecosystem categories, not role-level hiring volume or guaranteed employment.

source_summaries.name: Gameloft Nigeria careers and game-studio signal
source_summaries.scope: Nigeria game-studio and game-business career ecosystem
findings: Gameloft maintains a Nigeria careers presence and identifies studio, creative and business-development pathways.
source_summaries.limitations: The careers landing page is a studio signal, not a complete Nigerian vacancy census.

source_summaries.name: Jobberman Nigeria jobs
LinkedIn Nigeria game-design job-search snapshot
source_summaries.scope: Nigeria game-design and game-development search results
findings: The search surface included Nigerian and remote listings using titles such as game designer, game developer, Unity developer, Unreal gameplay developer and Python game developer.
source_summaries.limitations: A search-results page is a directional market signal, not a deduplicated vacancy dataset and not proof that all results remain open.

source_summaries.name: Maliyo Games Nigerian studio and career ecosystem
source_summaries.scope: Lagos-based mobile-game design, development, art, narrative and distribution
findings: Maliyo identifies Lagos as its headquarters and describes work spanning African stories, characters, environments, visuals, sound and mobile-game distribution.
The studio links to careers, GameUp Africa and junior-internship pathways.
source_summaries.limitations: Studio capability and career pathways do not imply that every named role is currently open.

source_summaries.name: MyJobMag Nigeria feeds
National Bureau of Statistics Nigeria Labour Force Survey
Nigerian Film Corporation creative-media National Occupational Standards workshop
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian creative-media trades including film, audio, content, photography, animation, graphics, broadcasting, gaming and immersive technologies
findings: The Nigerian Film Corporation reported a July 2026 critique and validation workshop intended to develop National Occupational Standards for creative-media trades, including film production, audio production, content creation, digital photography, animation, digital graphics, broadcasting, gaming and immersive technologies.
source_summaries.limitations: The workshop demonstrates Nigerian standardisation activity and named trade families; it does not mean final standards or a personal certificate already exist for every listed role.

source_summaries.name: Quantity Surveyors Registration Board of Nigeria 2024 newsletter
source_summaries.scope: Nigerian quantity-surveying practice and professional registration context
findings: The QSRBN newsletter supplies Nigerian quantity-surveying professional-body context and practice material.
source_summaries.limitations: The newsletter supports professional context; specific registration gates must be shown only where the applicable rule is explicit.

source_summaries.name: NCC and NITDA ICT ecosystem sources
University of Lagos Gamr Lab video-game development laboratory
source_summaries.scope: Nigeria game-development and esports training
findings: UNILAG describes Gamr Lab as a video-game development laboratory and talent hub opened in Lagos in March 2025.
The facility is intended to train game developers, designers and esports entrepreneurs and includes Unreal Engine, VR, motion-capture and high-end PC facilities.
source_summaries.limitations: A training facility is a capacity and pathway signal, not proof of a specific vacancy or salary.

source_summaries.name: Unreal Engine Lagos developer community
source_summaries.scope: Lagos real-time 3D, game, animation and immersive-development ecosystem
findings: The Lagos community page identifies a need to grow skills and training resources for games, animation and VFX and highlights Unreal Engine as a development tool.
source_summaries.limitations: Community participation does not establish a role requirement, employment count or certification gate.

source_summaries.name: Nigerian XR and immersive-technology ecosystem signals
source_summaries.scope: Lagos and Nigerian AR/VR/XR training, immersive media, education, healthcare and construction use cases
findings: Lagos XR ecosystem sources describe skills including 360 video, Unity, Unreal Engine, event planning and team leadership; local reporting also describes VR training and Nigerian immersive-technology education and emergency-services use cases.
source_summaries.limitations: These are ecosystem and training signals, not evidence of a national vacancy count or universal tool requirement.

source_summaries.name: National Bureau of Statistics Nigeria Labour Force Survey

source_summaries.scope: Nigerian vocational and technical pathways including garment making, leather work, furniture and upholstery, food and beverage service, industrial automation, AI, backend web, health and safety and other occupational standards
findings: NBTE's current NOS catalogue names occupational standards and levels for garment making, leather work, furniture and upholstery, food and beverage service, industrial automation, AI, backend web and other trades.
The Federal TVET initiative describes accredited centres, practical skills, employment and entrepreneurship pathways.
source_summaries.limitations: An NOS or TVET pathway is evidence of a Nigerian training route, not a claim that every employer requires the listed level or that one trade credential is interchangeable with a degree or professional licence.

findings: Government and NADDC sources describe nationwide automobile-maintenance, electric-vehicle, CNG and automotive software-capacity training.
ATCN describes Nigerian motorsport governance, driver/official training and an FIA engineering scholarship pathway.
source_summaries.limitations: These are sector training and ecosystem signals; they do not establish one universal automotive tool stack or a licence for every vehicle, motorsport or engineering role.

source_summaries.scope: Nigerian museum, archival, cultural and heritage certificate and diploma education
findings: The University of Ilorin announced 2025/2026 certificate and diploma programmes in museum and archival studies, cultural studies and creative arts.
source_summaries.limitations: An education certificate/diploma route is not a universal statutory licence or proof of demand for every heritage role.

source_summaries.scope: Nigerian music and entertainment business training, intellectual property and employability capacity building
findings: WIPO Nigeria described a 2024/2025 Music Business Academy scholarship and a nine-month vocational programme for African music-industry professionals.
source_summaries.limitations: This supports a sector training route, not a universal music-production certification or licence.

findings: The listing asks for Unity or Unreal Engine, C# or C++, 2D/3D graphics, prototyping, animation, testing, Git, documentation and a game portfolio.
The listing also mentions AR, VR and MR as adjacent technologies.
source_summaries.limitations: This is one vacancy and must not be treated as a national ranking or universal requirement.
